name: cloud-calc
description: Diego's Cloud Calc (#767) - an all-in-one calculator over libqalculate, the engine behind Qalculate!. Every number is computed by Cloud-Lib-Calc.apk (ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/calc), which this app BINDS after a contract handshake and never compiles (#763: an app compiles only what it renders). #770 three top-level sections (ui.sections) - Calculator, Measure and Jev - each a set of bottom-nav tabs, each tab a strip of modes declared below in ui.modes. Calculator: Calc (Standard, Scientific, Programmer, CAS, Physics & Constants), Convert (Units, Currency), Graph, Tools (Date & Time, Finance, Acoustics) and History; Measure: Sound (#772: meter/oscilloscope/tuner, Wave detection, History with waterfall and CSV/WAV export, Generator, What is it?), Camera (#772: Measure by reference object or ARCore, Level, Identify, Colour, Text-to-numbers - every image read by the shared image engine Cloud-Lib-ML-L-Image, on-device ML Kit by default or an OpenRouter decision model when Configs ▸ Image route says so) and Clock (World clock, Alarms, Timers, Stopwatch, Interval, Bedtime; #768); Jev (#770): Ask - a natural-language request routed by a decision model on OpenRouter's Decisions API to one of the app's own tools, which then computes - and Configs (Token, Routing, Models, Test). Any result can also be scored by a decision model (Ask about this result: calibrated probabilities, kept in History). A mode is DATA: its kind picks one of its renderers (expression, catalog, converter, form, plot, meter, history, and the six Clock kinds) and everything it shows - keys, options, forms, categories - is declared here. Offline by default: the network is used only by the engine's currency-rate download, on request, by the Jev section's and Sound ▸ What is it?'s calls to OpenRouter (build.json::jev; the shared libs:decisions client is the only code in this app that opens a URL), and - only when Configs ▸ Image route picks OpenRouter - by the image engine, which falls back to on-device ML Kit on any error; Calculator and Measure work without any of it, and the Clock section uses none (time zones are the device's tzdata, alarms are AlarmManager's). English is the base language (#299); dark is the default theme (#336).

android._doc_application_id: The fleet name with its separator dropped, as cloudc3 / clouddrive / cloudwallet.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.
auto_update._doc_enabled: Off because this app compiles no libs:updater (#763, see modules._doc): the Store updates it. Kept as data so the release block has the fleet's shape.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list. libs:calc is NOT here and must never be: it is the engine this app binds (engines.calc), and the engine contract guard (K6) fails the build if any module map points at it. #770 adds libs:text-tools, a `contract` lib (the token reader), which L4 does not count. #763: no `logic` lib is compiled in either — not libs:updater, not libs:analytics (lib-classes L4 holds the fleet's backlog of such edges and a new app may not add to it). Cloud Calc is installed and updated by the Store (SuperApp ▸ Constellation), like the 17 other apps that carry no updater.

clock._doc: #768 the Clock section's rules as a plain-JVM Kotlin module (clock/): alarm recurrence across repeat days and DST, timers, stopwatch laps, interval phases, what each AlarmManager wakeup does, and the stored JSON. No Android in it, so its suite runs without Robolectric and PIT mutation-tests it on every `gradle test` (clock/build.gradle). The Android half (AlarmManager, the foreground service, receivers, screens) is app/…/clock and ui/ClockScreens.kt.

jev._doc: #770 the Jev section's logic as a plain-JVM Kotlin module (jev/): the build.json::jev declaration's parser and validator, the Decisions API call (the app's ONLY network code: HttpURLConnection over Android's resolver, so the fleet DNS menu applies), the router (one choice question over the declared tools + none, thresholds, candidates, the offline fallback), reading numbers and durations out of a request, the per-field slot questions, follow-up questions about a result, and the live decision-model catalogue. No Android in it: its suite drives a real local HTTP server as the mock Decisions API, and PIT mutation-tests it on every `gradle test` (jev/build.gradle).

sound._doc: #772 the Sound tools' maths as a plain-JVM Kotlin module (sound/): the FFT, levels with A/C weighting and the calibration offset, YIN pitch and note names, the speed of sound and wavelength, wave detection (events gated over the buffer's own noise floor, named impulse/chirp/noise/tone/complex, with fundamental, harmonics, bandwidth, duration and envelope; spectral-flux onsets; periodicity), the tone/sweep/noise/dual/beats generator and its safe-volume guard, WAV and CSV, the waterfall's log bands, and the summary a decision model is sent for 'What is this sound?'. No Android in it: its suite runs golden signals and the generator-to-analyser loopback, and PIT mutation-tests it on every `gradle test` (sound/build.gradle). The microphone, the player and the screens are app/…/sound and ui/SoundScreens.kt.

measure._doc: #772 the Camera tools' maths as a plain-JVM Kotlin module (measure/): reference-object scaling of a photo (millimetres per pixel, lengths, paths, shoelace areas), the ARCore route's world geometry (distance, path, Newell polygon area, height), the inclinometer (tilt, pitch, roll and edge angle from gravity, against a stored zero) and the numbers OCR hands the calculator. Golden-geometry suite, PIT on every `gradle test`.

libs:ml-l-image._doc: #772 the CONTRACT half of the fleet's one image engine (engine-apk-split move 6), shared with Cloud Camera, Drive, Mail, Media Center and Office: the IImageScanEngine wire, the uniform Recognition result, recognition.json (THE image-recognition declaration: routes, thresholds, the OpenRouter model and categories) and the per-app route choice. Identify, Colour and Text run in Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Image-Mlkit.apk, which this app binds after a contract handshake and never compiles (a `contract` lib, no L4 edge).

libs:ml-l-sound._doc: #798 the CONTRACT half of the fleet's sound identification (ISoundEngine wire, SoundEngine client, sound.json: routes, thresholds, capture length), shared with Cloud Camera: 'What is this sound?' answers on device by default (YAMNet's 521 AudioSet classes), the decision model stays an optional route. YAMNet runs in Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Sound-Yamnet.apk, which this app binds after a contract handshake and never compiles (a `contract` lib, no L4 edge).

libs:decisions._doc: #772 OpenRouter's Decisions API client, lifted out of jev/ so the image engine (libs:ml-l-image-mlkit) speaks the same protocol: a `contract` lib (the thin client of a remote engine), so no L4 edge. jev/ binds it to build.json::jev; the app reads Http/Decision through it.

libs:databackend._doc_dir: #825 the engine wire (IDataBackend + DataBackendClient/Service), out of libs:core so a wire edit rebuilds only the engines and the apps that bind one.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which is what makes this app a fleet mesh member with the debug API (/api/calc/* below) without per-app wiring.

libs:bottomnav._doc_dir: The fleet bottom-nav island: this app supplies its own five entries from ui.tabs (BottomNavEntry/BottomNavIsland/bottomNavInsets/rememberBottomNavCollapse), never cloud-mail's bottomNavItems.

libs:text-tools._doc: #770 the ITextTools binder (contract class in 1_cicd/src/data/lib-classes.json, so no L4 backlog edge), shared BY REFERENCE: the Jev section reads the OpenRouter token the fleet Account manages through TextToolsClient.revealAiKey("openrouter") - the SuperApp's Profile pushes the vault's ai.tokens into the serving app over the same CONSTELLATION_DATA-guarded binder - so the token has one store and this app keeps no copy of it. A manual override lives only in this app's Keystore-backed EncryptedSharedPreferences.

engines._doc: THE ENGINE THIS APP BINDS INSTEAD OF COMPILING (the ac_cloud-news shape). `fleet` is the Store row the package is resolved from at build time (an unknown id fails the build) for BuildConfig and <queries>; `action` finds the service ({package} substituted, matching the engine manifest's ${applicationId}.ENGINE); `min_contract` is the lowest engine CONTRACT that answers every method CalcClient calls, read through PackageManager BEFORE binding.

jev._doc: #770 THE ONE declaration of Cloud Calc's decision-model layer (jev/JevConfig.kt parses and validates it; the router, the Configs screens and /api/jev/config all read it). app/build.gradle bakes it into BuildConfig.JEV_CONFIG_B64; Configs > Routing may replace it with the user's own edit of this same JSON (stored in SharedPreferences, validated by the same parser, Reset drops it). A decision model only SCORES options - it never computes: every number is still the app's engines' (libqalculate through Cloud-Lib-Calc, the Clock engine). Endpoint/model/question shapes verified against openrouter.ai/docs/guides/community/jev and the Decisions API reference on 2026-10-02 (questions are a MAP of typed questions: noul -> answers.<q>.noul; choice -> choice + probabilities; score -> score + probabilities by level index + legend; usage.cost in USD).
jev._models_url_doc: The live catalogue of decision models. No model list is spelled anywhere in this app: Configs > Models shows what this returns (cached for catalog_ttl_hours). On 2026-10-02 it returned typesafe/jev-1.13, ~typesafe/jev-latest, liquid/d1, inception/mercury-decide:free, upstage/solar-decide, respan/span-01, respan/span-01-lite, respan/span-01-lite:free, togethercomputer/tev1-4b-experimental and jaredpalmer/kev-4b, all text-only; cloudflare/clef and cloudflare/clef-flash were NOT in it. An image can be attached as state only when the chosen model's catalogue entry lists image among its input_modalities.
jev._key_url_doc: Configs > Token's Test button: GET with the token, which answers the key's label and usage without spending anything.
jev._account_provider_doc: The provider id the fleet Account's token is read under: Configs > Token reads it with libs:text-tools TextToolsClient.revealAiKey(account_provider) over the CONSTELLATION_DATA-guarded ITextTools binder, the path the SuperApp's Profile writes the vault's ai.tokens through (aa_cloud-superapp build.json ai_tokens: openrouter_my_ai_api -> openrouter). It is read on use and never stored by this app; a manual override, if the user sets one, lives only in this app's Keystore-backed EncryptedSharedPreferences and wins while set.

uses._doc: Which model each use runs on: a slug, or "cheapest" = the cheapest model the cached catalogue confirms (a :free variant first among equals). A declared slug the catalogue does not list falls back to the cheapest confirmed one, so a retired model never breaks the app; with no catalogue cached yet the slug is used as declared. Configs > Models overrides either use per device.

jev._doc_use_labels: What Configs > Models calls each use in `uses`; a use with no label shows its id.

route._doc: Jev mode. One Decisions request per typed request: the choice question `route` over `tools` + none (none_criterion), plus `questions` (shown with their probabilities). P(pick) >= threshold routes; a confident none says so; below threshold the top `candidates` tools with P >= candidate_min_p are offered to pick from. Any failure (no token, network, HTTP, malformed answer, a probability outside [0,1], a pick outside the set) applies on_error: expression = evaluate the request, lead-in phrases stripped, in fallback_mode (libqalculate reads '3 ft to cm' itself), none = say why. A form tool's numbers are read from the request; with two or more fields a second request asks, per field, which number it is (slot_instructions, {field} = the field label), and a field whose pick is none or below slot_threshold keeps its declared default.
route.instructions: Which one of this calculator app's tools would answer `request`? Pick none when it asks for something a calculator, unit converter, measurement or timer cannot do.
route.none_criterion: The request is not a calculation, conversion, measurement or timer: conversation, an opinion, or a fact that needs no computing.

tools._doc: The options offered to the model: id -> {criterion (what the model reads), action, mode (a ui.modes id), form (a form id of that mode)}. action expression = the request text, lead-ins stripped, evaluated with that mode's engine options; form = numbers into that form's fields, its outputs evaluated; timer = a Clock timer for the duration named; open = show that mode. DeclarationsTest holds every mode/form named here to ui.modes.

arithmetic.criterion: Plain arithmetic or percentages: a number expression to evaluate, e.g. 15% of 42 or 2^10 / 3.

scientific.criterion: Trigonometry, logarithms, roots, factorials or other scientific functions.

programmer.criterion: Number bases (hex, binary, octal) or bitwise operations.

algebra.criterion: Solve an equation, differentiate, integrate, factor or simplify a symbolic expression.

units.criterion: Convert a quantity between units: length, mass, volume, temperature, speed, energy, pressure, data size or other physical units.

currency.criterion: Convert an amount of money between currencies.

discount.criterion: A price after a percentage discount, or how much a discount saves.

tip.criterion: A tip on a restaurant bill: the tip, the total, or the total split per person.

loan.criterion: The monthly payment of a loan or mortgage from its principal, annual rate and years.

interest.criterion: Compound interest: what a sum grows to at an annual rate over years.

db_sum.criterion: Add two sound levels in decibels (a dB sum).

sound_speed.criterion: The speed of sound in air at a temperature.

wavelength.criterion: The wavelength or period of a sound frequency.

db_ratio.criterion: Express a power or amplitude ratio in decibels.

db_distance.criterion: The sound level at another distance from a source.

timer.criterion: Start a countdown timer for a duration.

alarm.criterion: Set or check an alarm for a time of day.

world_clock.criterion: The current time in another city or time zone.

sound_meter.criterion: Measure how loud it is around the phone with its microphone.

questions._doc: Extra questions sent in the same request as `route`; their probabilities are shown beside the pick. Any noul, choice or score question may be added here.

computable.label: Computable
computable.instructions: `request` asks for something a calculator app can compute, convert, measure or time.

criteria.true: It names a calculation, a conversion, a measurement or a duration.
criteria.false: It is conversation or a question no computation answers.

jev._doc_identify: #772 'What is this?' per measurement kind. A decision model cannot hear: the Sound tools send what THIS app measured (level, fundamental and note, dominant frequency, every detected event's kind, duration, bandwidth, noisiness, harmonics, attack and decay, onsets, periodicity; :sound Session.describe) as state, and ask one choice over `classes` (question id "class") plus the extra noul/score `questions`. A spectrogram image rides along only when the model's catalogue entry takes images. Every option's probability is shown; nothing is decided for the user. The model per use is uses.sound (Configs > Models can override it).

sound.instructions: Which kind of sound source best explains these measurements of a sound recorded by a phone microphone? `measured` lists the overall level, the fundamental and its musical note, the dominant frequency, and each detected event with its kind (tone, chirp, noise, impulse, complex), duration, bandwidth, noisiness (0 = pure tone, 1 = white noise), harmonics relative to the fundamental, attack and decay times, plus onsets and whether the events repeat periodically.

classes.speech: Human speech or voice: voiced harmonics around 85-300 Hz, syllable-rate onsets, irregular events.
classes.music: Music or singing: stable pitched tones with harmonics, notes changing over time, often rhythmic.
classes.birdsong: Birdsong: short high chirps or whistles, typically 1-8 kHz, fast frequency sweeps.
classes.dog: A dog barking: loud short harmonic bursts around 300-1500 Hz, repeated irregularly.
classes.siren: A siren: a loud tone sweeping slowly up and down in a repeating cycle.
classes.alarm: An alarm, beeper or smoke detector: a loud steady or pulsed tone, often 2-4 kHz, strictly periodic.
classes.engine: An engine or motor vehicle: low-frequency broadband rumble with a periodic firing tone.
classes.fan: A fan, HVAC or air conditioning: steady broadband noise with a constant low hum, no onsets.
classes.mains_hum: Electrical mains hum: a steady low tone at 50 or 60 Hz or its harmonics (100/120 Hz).
classes.water: Running water, rain or a tap: steady broadband noise, flat spectrum, many tiny impulses.
classes.wind: Wind: low-frequency broadband noise with slow level fluctuations.
classes.tool: A power tool or machine: loud harmonic whine with broadband noise, steady while running.
classes.knock: A knock, clap, footstep or impact: short impulses with a sharp attack and fast decay.
classes.silence: Silence or near silence: very low level and no events.
classes.other: Something else, or too ambiguous to say.

questions._doc: Asked alongside the class, with their probabilities.

natural.label: Natural?
natural.instructions: The sound comes from a natural source (an animal, a person, weather, water) rather than a machine or a device.

attention.label: Needs attention?
attention.instructions: How much attention does a sound like this usually call for from someone nearby?

ask._doc: Addendum A: the preset follow-up questions offered under a result, by mode id; "*" is offered under every mode. The state the model scores is {mode, calculation, result, context?} - the result is always the app's own; the model only rates it in its context. Each is a Decisions question (noul / choice with criteria / score with levels lowest first) plus a chip `label`. A free question box is always offered too: yes/no by default, or a choice or a scale over options the user types.

*.label: Plausible?
*.instructions: How plausible is `result` as the outcome of `calculation` in `mode`, for the situation in `context` when there is one?

*.label: Size
*.instructions: How large is `result` compared with everyday values of the quantity `calculation` produces?

criteria.small: Smaller than everyday values of this kind.
criteria.typical: A typical everyday value of this kind.
criteria.large: Larger than everyday values of this kind.

acoustics.label: Hearing-safe?
acoustics.instructions: A sound at the level given by `result` (in dB) is safe for unprotected human hearing over an hour of exposure.

meter.label: Hearing-safe?
meter.instructions: A sound at the level given by `result` is safe for unprotected human hearing over an hour of exposure.

finance.label: Reasonable tip?
finance.instructions: `result`, from `calculation`, is a reasonable amount for its purpose (a tip, a discount, a loan payment) in most countries.

units.label: Normal range?
units.instructions: `result` is within the normal everyday range for the quantity converted in `calculation`.

_doc_sound: #772 THE ONE declaration of the Sound tools (Measure ▸ Sound). sample_rate is the capture and playback rate. analysis is :sound Analysis.Params, every threshold of wave detection: frame/hop (FFT frames, samples), block (the envelope and gate resolution), fmin/fmax and yin_threshold (pitch), gate_db over the buffer's own noise floor (10th percentile of block levels) with silence_db as the absolute floor, min_event_ms and merge_gap_ms (segmentation), impulse_ms/impulse_decay_ms, noise_flatness, tone_stability and chirp_change (the event kinds), periodic_cv (a train of events), harmonics (how many are measured), onset_k/onset_window/onset_delta/onset_rise_db (spectral-flux onsets). defaults seed the three per-device knobs the user can change on any sound screen: calibration_db (added to every dBFS level; a phone microphone is uncalibrated, so 0 means relative), a4_hz (the tuning reference of note names) and temperature_c (the speed of sound behind every wavelength). record_ms is how long Wave detection and What is it? listen. history: refresh_ms between readings, max_samples kept, waterfall rows and log bands from fmin_hz, max_wav_seconds of raw audio kept for the WAV export. generator: the safe-volume guard (max_amplitude of full scale; above loud_volume of the device's media volume the cap drops to loud_amplitude), the frequency band, the beat limit, max_ms, the fade, and the screen's defaults. identify.spectrogram is the image size sent to a decision model whose catalogue entry takes images.
_doc_camera: #772 THE ONE declaration of the Camera tools (Measure > Camera). references: the objects of known size the photo route scales by, each one edge's length in millimetres (ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 for a bank card, ISO 216 for A4, the issuing mint's diameter for a coin). capture: the longest side and JPEG quality a photo is kept at. level: the bubble's tolerance and how often the sensor is read. colour: the square of pixels a tapped colour averages. ocr.send_to_mode: the expression mode a recognised number is sent to. ar: whether the ARCore route is offered when the phone has ARCore.

ui._doc: EVERY list this app renders. app/build.gradle bakes ui.* into BuildConfig as base64 JSON and Declarations.kt decodes it once; no tab id, mode id, key or form is spelled in Kotlin.
ui._doc_sections: #868 THE ONE navigation declaration (libs:bottomnav's NavDecl), INVERTED from #770: ui.bottom_nav is the island's section ids in display order, ui.sections[] are Calculator, Measure and Jev, each with `pages` - the ten tabs (what #770 called ui.tabs), drawn as the section's top PageTabs strip - and ui.default_section is where the app opens (its first page). Calculator = the traditional calculators (#767), Measure = sensors and the clock & timers (#768), Jev = natural-language requests routed by a decision model, and its Configs. A page shows the modes whose `tab` is its id, in ui.modes order, as the sub-strip under the page strip. test/test-calc-shell.sh fails on a section with no page, a page with no mode and a mode naming no page.
ui._doc_modes: One entry per mode. `kind` picks the renderer: expression (input + autocomplete + keypad + result), catalog (engine items listed by category, tap to evaluate), converter (value + from/to units of an engine category), form (declared fields substituted into declared expressions), plot (y = f(x) sampled by the engine), meter (microphone level + spectrum; the permission is asked only when this mode opens), history (past results and the engine's own variables). `options` is the engine's eval options JSON (libs/calc EvalOptions: in_base, out_base, precision, angle, approx 0 exact/1 exact where possible/2 decimal, mixed_units, unicode). A key is a string inserted as typed, or {label, insert}; the labels AC, DEL and = are the three actions. #768 the Clock tab adds six kinds whose data is the mode's `clock` object: worldclock (`zones`, the cities shown until the user edits the list; any id of the device's tzdata), alarms (`snooze_choices`/`snooze_default` minutes, `ring_minutes` before a ring silences itself, `vibrate_default`), timers (`presets` in seconds), stopwatch, interval (`presets`: work/rest/long_rest seconds, `long_every` rounds, `rounds`), bedtime (`sleep_choices` minutes for the sleep timer, which stops other apps' playback by taking audio focus; `bedtime_default` for the nightly reminder, a quiet alarm). Clock state lives in SharedPreferences `cloud_clock`, every wakeup is an AlarmManager alarm re-planned from it on boot, update and time/zone change, and a foreground service keeps anything running visible and controllable with the app closed. #770 the Jev section adds five kinds whose data is build.json::jev, not the mode: jev (type a request; the routing decision with every option's probability, then the picked tool's result computed by this app's engines, or the top candidates to pick from when the model is unsure), jev_token (the OpenRouter token: the fleet Account's by default, a masked manual override in Keystore-backed storage, a Test button), jev_routing (the routing table - tools, questions, thresholds, fallback - shown and editable as the JSON the router itself reads, with reset to defaults), jev_models (the live decision-model catalogue and the per-use model choice) and jev_test (one prompt against one or several models side by side: the raw request with the token redacted, every option's probability, latency and cost). #772 the Sound tab adds four kinds whose data is build.json::sound, not the mode: sound_events (listen, then events named impulse/chirp/noise/tone/complex with their features, onsets, periodicity), sound_history (a running session: waterfall, level/frequency/wavelength over time, saved as CSV/WAV and exported through the system file picker), sound_generator (tones, sweeps, noise, dual tone, beats behind the safe-volume guard; no microphone) and sound_identify (the measurements, never the audio, sent to the sound model with build.json::jev.identify.sound's classes; every probability shown). The microphone is asked for only by a listening sound mode, through ui/SoundScreens.kt's MicGate. #772 the Camera tab adds five kinds whose data is build.json::camera: camera_measure (ARCore distance/path/area/height when ARCore is available, else a photo measured against a reference object of known size from `references`, with calibration), camera_level (inclinometer from the gravity sensor, `level`), camera_identify (a photo recognised by the shared image engine on the route Configs ▸ Image route picks; labels, boxes and the object count, every probability shown), camera_colour (tap a point: hex, RGB, HSL and the engine's colour name over `colour.sample_px`) and camera_text (OCR, numbers sent to `ocr.send_to_mode`); image_route (Configs) picks the route - on-device ML Kit or an OpenRouter decision model - and the model, per app. The camera is asked for only by a Camera mode that takes a photo, through ui/CameraScreens.kt's CameraGate.

modes.label: Physics & Constants
modes._doc: The CODATA constants are libqalculate's own (variables.xml); the categories are its category titles, so nothing is restated here.

modes.label: Units
modes._doc: Unit categories are libqalculate's own category titles (units.xml); the units in each come from the engine at run time (items unit <category>), so ~600 units appear with no list here.

modes.label: Currency
modes._doc: The ONLY network use in the app: `rates` shows the age of the rates the engine has and a button that asks it to fetch fresh ones (CalcEngine.fetchRates, through Android's resolver so the DNS menu applies). Until then the rates compiled into libqalculate are used, and their date is shown.

modes.label: Sound meter
modes._doc: Microphone level, waveform and spectrum, computed in THIS process: audio capture is granted per package (RECORD_AUDIO), so the engine's process could not record (the libs:contacts boundary, #763 `pinned`). Asked for only when a listening sound mode opens. #772 the meter is also the oscilloscope and tuner: dB with A and C weighting, sample peak, dominant frequency, fundamental with note and cents, wavelength. The sample rate and the calibration offset are build.json::sound's (one knob for every sound mode); this object keeps only what is the meter's own.

modes.label: Wave detection
modes._doc: #772 listen for build.json::sound.record_ms, then cut the buffer into events and name each (impulse, chirp, noise, tone, complex) with its fundamental, harmonics, bandwidth, duration and envelope; onsets and periodicity of the whole. The thresholds are build.json::sound.analysis.

modes.label: History
modes._doc: #772 a running session: a scrolling spectrogram (waterfall) plus graphs over time of the level, the dominant/fundamental frequency and its wavelength at the declared speed of sound. Saved as CSV (and WAV while the audio fits build.json::sound.history.max_wav_seconds) in the app's own storage, and exported anywhere the user picks, the Cloud Drive store included.

modes.label: Generator
modes._doc: #772 tones (sine/square/triangle/saw), sweeps, white/pink noise, dual tone and beats, behind the safe-volume guard in build.json::sound.generator.

modes.label: What is it?
modes._doc: #772 listen, measure, and ask a decision model which of build.json::jev.identify.sound's classes the measurements describe (the model never hears the audio; a spectrogram image rides along only for a model whose catalogue entry takes images). Every class's probability and the extra questions' are shown; offline it still shows what was measured.

modes.label: Measure
modes._doc: #772 lengths, paths, areas and heights. With ARCore on the phone: tap points in the live scene (anchors on detected planes) for distance, path, area and height, in metres. Without it: a photo and a reference object of known size (build.json::camera.references, or a length the user measured) gives millimetres per pixel - true in the reference's own plane, square to the camera, which the screen says.

modes.label: Level
modes._doc: #772 the inclinometer: tilt, pitch, roll and the edge angle from the gravity sensor, against a zero the user sets on a reference surface; a bubble that turns green within build.json::camera.level.tolerance_deg. No camera, no network.

modes.label: Identify
modes._doc: #772 a photo through the shared image-recognition engine (libs:ml-l-image, the route the user picked in Jev > Configs > Image route: on-device ML by default, or an OpenRouter decision model that falls back to on-device): labels with probabilities, object boxes and their count, colours, text, and the decision model's extra questions. The count can be corrected by hand.

modes.label: Colour
modes._doc: #772 tap a photo: the colour under the finger (the mean of build.json::camera.colour.sample_px square) as hex, RGB and HSL, named by the image engine in recognition.json's vocabulary.

modes.label: Text
modes._doc: #772 OCR a photo through the image engine; every number found is a chip that sends itself, or their sum, to the calculator (build.json::camera.ocr.send_to_mode).

modes.label: Image route
modes._doc: #772 Configs > Image recognition route: On-device ML (the default, offline) or an OpenRouter decision model, and that model, picked from the live decision catalogue the image engine reads. The choice is this app's (RecognitionPrefs); the routes, thresholds and the default model are libs:ml-l-image/recognition.json, shared with Cloud Camera.

ui._doc_debug_api: The routes this app adds to the fleet debug API (libs:devtools AppDebugServer), so a calculation can be checked with the screen locked: /api/calc/eval?expr=&mode= evaluates through the bound engine with that mode's options, /api/calc/modes lists ui.modes, /api/calc/info is the engine handshake + engine info. #768 the Clock section registers a second group, build.json::ui.debug_api.clock_group (/api/clock/*), so alarms and timers can be checked and driven with the screen locked: status (every alarm, timer, the stopwatch, interval, sleep timer and what is ringing, each with its planned wakeup and whether AlarmManager really holds a PendingIntent for it, plus canScheduleExactAlarms and the system's next alarm clock), timer_start?seconds=&label= / timer_cancel?id= (a real timer through the same engine the screen uses), alarm_add?time=HH:MM&days=&label= / alarm_delete?id=, dismiss?key=. The op is `status`, not `state`: 1_cicd/src/data/update-ack-guard.json owns the `state` branch key of every `when (op)` route table for GET /api/state. #770 a third group, build.json::ui.debug_api.jev_group (/api/jev/*): route?q= (the routing decision, the chosen tool and its result as computed by this app; a timer only starts with run=1; never the token) and config (the routing table in force, whether it is the default or the user's edit, the models per use, and where the token comes from - masked). #772 the Sound tools register build.json::ui.debug_api.sound_group (/api/sound/*), a loopback self-test with the screen locked: generate?f=440&ms=500 (&kind, wave, f2, amp) plays a guarded tone and keeps its samples; analyze?ms=1000 records the microphone (source=mic, the default) or re-reads the last generated buffer (source=generator, no microphone at all) and reports the detected frequency, note, level and events; status reports the permission, the last generation, the history session and the saved sessions. A recording from a background app is silenced by Android, and analyze says so (silenced: true) rather than reporting a frequency of nothing.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds.

unit._doc: Every project's `test`: the JVM suites in app/src/test (the declaration parser against this build.json, every pure per-mode function, Robolectric suites per section incl. #772 SoundAppTest and CameraAppTest) plus the plain-JVM modules clock, jev, sound and measure and the shared libs:decisions / libs:ml-l-image, each JVM module followed by its PIT mutation gate.
